form: Open coiled capital G with an interior bar. Its connected upper flourish is not a separate tilde. Use the same ordinary G rendering throughout; the genuine detached tilde on G_3 in 029 remains. This resolves the initial 026–027 alternative, without changing the written J versus 3 indices.

Roman graph/groupoid names generally have common upper and lower horizontal strokes. Render those explicitly where seen. The two II forms on 027 also have distinct pointed hats; the III in 028 has no such hat. Keep the unframed V in 039. Framing is not interpreted as a completion operation.

Omega is a two-lobed w-like stroke. A detached short tick is a prime. Keep the written position of primes, especially 040 (71)–(72); retain cancelled/overwritten ticks as doubtful rather than inventing stars.

Path tildes are separate accents. Preserve local absent tildes and the source's differing inverse-path notation. The angular small alpha accent in 028 is a tilde by the locally defined notation; the isolated hat in 035 is kept as written.
The curved entrance of live gamma on 027 is part of the letter, not a minus. The crossed draft at (24) has a separate minus. Here p is Latin p, not rho.

Angular upper stroke and one long lower curve. Final cross-page comparison reads the parameter introduced in 030 consistently as zeta, including primed/subscripted forms. C's xi spelling in this run is corrected; this does not resolve the unrelated buried xi-like cancellations on 026/029.

Automorphism letters and inverse exponents remain distinct. The question rho inverse? on 031 and the cancellations on 036–039 are retained. The overwritten operator in 031 (43) remains sigma/tau uncertain.
Capital Pi with the 0,3 subscript is distinguished from the local lower-case pi notation. Hats and base-point subscripts are retained individually; no completion marker is supplied by expectation.
The later component and fundamental-groupoid symbols have capital Pi, rather than H's occasional lower-case pi.
Two upright strokes and a crossbar in all six exponents of the right marginal substitutions. It is not mu or an adjacent multiplicative factor.

Three two-element orientation/component sets in 044 (3). The first has an upper bar as well as an underline; cyclic-order omega has no upper bar. The overwritten second orientation-set glyph on 050 remains explicitly barred/unbarred uncertain. The clear opening form on 051 has both strokes.

Keep visible index position and alphabet differences: raised omega in 050 (16), lowered i-omega in its live explanatory line, capital J at the end of 044, and I in 046 (10) and 047 (12). These are not homogenized.
The punctured sphere, projective blow-up, cut surface and its interior carry distinct written modifiers. None is replaced by the other because a later identification is asserted.
The stars and the second quotient's plus are distinct written signs in the projective/tangent-direction annotations. No expansion of the star notation is substituted into the manuscript.
The left NB uses a parenthesized raised epsilon and a crossed lower epsilon-like remnant at both occurrences.
Upper inserted cutting notation Dec has medium confidence; the later body occurrence has a visible dotted i and is read Dic. Neither an accent nor uniform spelling is supplied.
Written equality can abbreviate même/mêmes. Preserve the sign and its written s; distinguish this from equality in a displayed formula.
Paired ordinary quotation strokes are represented by two opening backticks and two closing apostrophes, following the supplied convention.

Retain local cancellation scope and insertion attachment. A rounded frame or a shared Roman-numeral bar is not an erasure. Conversely a hatched old symbol is not omitted because its replacement is legible.
